passage:
'Can you check the folder once more?' Karthik asked.
Sabina flipped through it on the hostel common-room table. 'Resume, marksheets, ID. Same as the last three times.'
'Okay. Okay.' He muttered under his breath, 'Good morning, thank you for having me, I'm interested in this role because...'
'You've said that line forty times.'
'What if I blank? What if they ask about the gap semester?'
'Then you tell them what you told me. You were fine.'
'Will you come with me tomorrow? Just sit in the lobby.'
Sabina hesitated. 'I've got a lab at ten.'
'Please. If you're there I'll be calm.' He zipped the folder, then unzipped it to check the ID again. 'See? This is why I need you there.'
Sabina sighed and nodded. Karthik breathed out, and for a minute his shoulders dropped.

qa.q: What does Sabina say is in the folder?
What does Karthik believe will happen if Sabina isn't there?
qa.a: He believes he won't be calm without Sabina, as if the interview is only safe with a helper beside him.

qa.q: What could Karthik try at this stage instead of more checking?
qa.a: He could pack the folder once, practise a couple of answers and go alone, letting the nerves rise and fall so he learns he can manage without the safety habits.

qa.q: What is it like for Sabina to be asked to skip the lab?
qa.a: Sabina wants to help but feels torn, and each check and request may leave Sabina tired and unsure whether saying yes really helps him.

grounding: It shows a young man checking, rehearsing and asking a friend to come along, each habit bringing brief calm while confirming the danger.

passage:
Last semester I built a whole system without noticing. Before every class presentation I'd write out every sentence, even the jokes. I'd sit by the door in case I needed to leave. I'd carry two water bottles. And I'd call Gurleen five minutes before, so she could say, 'You'll be fine, Kishore.'
Every time, it worked. I'd get through, sweaty but alive, and think: thank god I did all that.
It took me months to see the trap. I never gave myself the chance to find out I'd have been fine without the script or the call. Every presentation 'proved' that presenting was dangerous and that only my rituals kept me safe.
Last week Gurleen was in a lecture and didn't pick up. I stood outside the room, frozen, thinking: now what?

qa.q: Where would Kishore sit before a presentation?
qa.a: Kishore would sit by the door in case of needing to leave.

qa.q: Why did Kishore feel grateful for the rituals after every presentation?
qa.a: Getting through felt like proof that the script, the water and the call had kept Kishore safe, so the relief got attached to the rituals.

qa.q: What could Kishore try next, now that the trap is visible?
qa.a: Kishore could drop one safety habit at a time, the full script first, and present with the fear, learning that it passes without the ritual.

qa.q: How might Gurleen feel on seeing the missed call after the lecture?
qa.a: Gurleen might feel a jolt of worry or guilt, realising how much Kishore had been leaning on that one call.

grounding: It shows someone relying on scripts, an exit seat and a reassuring call, each bringing brief calm but confirming that presenting felt dangerous.
